scope: Proposition 19.1 (Energy of the comparison metric) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 113. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (f, t) be the global solutions of Equation (17.6) supplied by Proposition 17.3, and let e gn = e4ϵĝn and the comparison fields be as in Proposition 18.4. In the normalized end coordinates z = e2ϵy, these data satisfy e gn − δ = O2(|z|−1 ), e X1,n, e X2,n = O1(|z|−2 ), Re gn ∈ L1 (X, dVe gn ). Their ADM energies are finite and obey (19.1) e En ≤ e2ϵ (E∗ + ηn), ηn ≥ 0, ηn −→ 0. No uniform bound in n on the solutions’ classical regularity constants is needed for this conclusion.
